evidence.snippet: The monday.com platform API utilizes personal V2 API tokens to authenticate requests
Admins and Guests cannot access an API key but can utilize API features through other authentication methods, like OAuth

decisions.reason: Pages confirm personal tokens sent as bearer-style Authorization header plus a documented OAuth2 app flow, so both methods are supported.

evidence.snippet: Monday requires the OAuth app to be installed in the target workspace before users can authorize their accounts
A Monday workspace admin only needs to install the app once per workspace
Admins and Guests cannot access an API key but can utilize API features through other authentication methods, like OAuth

decisions.reason: While personal API tokens are self-serve, the OAuth app path (needed for multi-user/production integrations) requires a workspace admin to install the app first, making admin_scope the real friction point.

evidence.snippet: If you don't have a monday.com account yet, create a free developer account to get an API token and start testing
A Monday workspace admin only needs to install the app once per workspace. After the admin approves the installation, users in that workspace can connect their Monday accounts normally.

decisions.reason: A developer can self-serve a personal token to build immediately, but production OAuth-based integrations require workspace-admin app installation, so it's buildable with caveats rather than fully frictionless.
